title: Report
description: A human- and machine-consumable presentation of an analysis. The schema's central requirement is structural separation: observed facts, inferred relationships, verification outcomes, confidence, unknown information and errors occupy distinct sections and can never be merged. This is what stops a report from presenting an inference in the same voice as an observation, which is the failure mode that makes provenance tooling untrustworthy.

boundary.description: The observation boundary the reported analysis was made at.

sections.description: The report body, separated by epistemic status. Every section is required, even when empty: an absent section and an empty section mean different things, and only one of them is honest.

observedFacts.description: Statements directly supported by evidence of a record that exists, with no inference. Every entry requires evidence.

inferredRelationships.description: Relationships that were derived rather than observed. Kept separate from observed facts, and each entry must state the basis of the inference. The entry schema is defined separately from the statement schema rather than composed from it, so that inferenceBasis is structurally required here and structurally rejected on an observed fact.

verification.description: The verification outcome for each subject that was checked.

confidence.description: Confidence values assigned in this report, with the evidence each derives from.

unknown.description: Questions the analysis could not answer, each with the reason. This section exists so that a report can be complete about its own incompleteness instead of omitting what it could not determine.

question.description: The question that could not be answered, stated as a question.

errors.description: Errors encountered during analysis. Required because a report that silently absorbs its own failures is worse than one that fails outright: it produces a plausible document from partial data.

relationshipFindings.description: Explanations of why each important relationship exists, so that a reader does not have to reconstruct the reasoning from the evidence set.

observationallySupported.description: Whether the relationship was directly observed. A relationship explained only by inference must say so on the finding itself, not only in the section it appears under.

disclaimers.description: Statements that must accompany the report. Rule provenance/evidence-traceability requires the non-security-determination disclaimer to be present, so that an implementation cannot emit a report that reads as a security assessment.

truncated.description: Whether any part of the reported analysis was bounded before exhaustion.

statement.description: One statement a report makes about something observed, with the evidence that supports it.

evidence.description: Evidence supporting the statement. Required and non-empty: a report statement without evidence is an unsupported assertion, which is the thing this specification exists to prevent.

inferredStatement.description: One statement a report makes about a relationship it derived rather than observed. Identical to a statement except that inferenceBasis is required, and the field list is restated here rather than composed with $ref because a composed schema with additionalProperties false would reject the very field that makes the entry inferred.

evidence.description: Evidence supporting the inference, which is necessarily evidence of the inputs to the inference rather than of its conclusion.

inferenceBasis.description: Why the relationship was inferred rather than observed, for example a digest equality consistent with a derivation or an interface shape consistent with a declared dependency. Required, so an inference cannot be presented in the same voice as an observation.
